podcast.body: This song from the album "Ágætis byrjun" is described as lovely and indicative of Sigur Rós's dreamy sound, with its title potentially referencing "sleepwalkers and angels." It is emblematic of their unique approach to music.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track, translated as "Sleepwalking Angels," is derived from an Icelandic pun that only locals would understand. It runs over 10 minutes on the album and over 9 minutes as a single. "My favorite track from the album is a song that translates as Sleepwalking Angels, but is actually derived from a pun that only people from Iceland will understand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What Exactly is Post Rock? Part 2
